To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there were differences among how adolescents perceived discussions about the conflict with their families depending upon their parent's behaviors and communication styles.

adolescents who perceive their mothers as authoritative have the most positive perception of their discussions about the civil war in Northern Ireland, and that adolescents who perceive themselves as being in the authoritarian parenting practice category have the most negative perception of their discussions.

the majority of the adolescents in the study were raised in an authoritative parenting practice and their discussions about the conflict of Northern Ireland were more positive and less tense than the other parenting styles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of parenting practices and communication patterns within family systems in the context of Northern Ireland's civil conflict.
the role that family communication patterns play in the development of adolescents in Northern Ireland.
the impact of the family environment and communication patterns on the development of adolescent perceptions of civil conflict.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there are no significant differences in the way adolescents perceive their parents and the level of tension in the home as a result of their discussions about the civil conflicts of Northern Ireland based on parenting style.

the parenting style of authoritative parenting practices, as defined by Baumrind (1966) and Maccoby and Martin (1983), was the most prevalent in the sample and that adolescents in the authoritative parenting practices category reported more tension with their mothers and fathers than adolescents from other parenting styles.
the results of this study do not support the Family Communication Patterns and Baumrind theories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a significant relationship between parenting practices and adolescents' perceptions of conversations about civil conflict.
there is not a significant difference in adolescent's perception of conflict discussions with their mothers depending on their parenting style.

the parenting practices of adolescents' parents are associated with how adolescents perceive their parents, and how they perceive their parents is associated with their perceptions of the political conflict of Northern Ireland.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parenting practices and styles can have a direct impact on the way in which parents communicate about sensitive topics such as political/social conflict.
parenting styles do matter, and they matter in the context of conflict.
there is a need to understand how the family influences the development of the adolescent's political identity.
